title: Build Tools: Vite, Webpack & esbuild
nestedConcepts: Choose a build tool for the project

subtopics.title: Development server
subtopics.explanation: A development server serves source files and refreshes the page while you work. It can show errors quickly, but does not behave exactly like the final production build.

subtopics.title: Transform
subtopics.explanation: A transform step converts files the browser or target environment can use. It can handle TypeScript, JSX, modern syntax, and CSS imports. Keep a clear browser support target so the tool does not do unnecessary work.

subtopics.title: Bundle
subtopics.explanation: A bundler follows imports and connects related files. It can combine small files, split separate routes, and emit names that change when file contents change.

subtopics.title: Optimize the production build
subtopics.explanation: Production tools can remove unused code, minify text, compress assets, and split output into chunks. Each change affects the files users download, so inspect a real production build. Measure load behavior and verify that required code and styles still appear after optimization.

subtopics.title: Choose a build tool for the project
subtopics.explanation: Vite, Webpack, and esbuild overlap but differ in development workflow, plugin support, and configuration. Choose based on the app’s needs, the team’s experience, and deployment constraints. A familiar tool with the needed integrations is often better than adopting a tool for a small benchmark win.

foundations.overview: Build tools connect, transform, and prepare source files for browsers.
foundations.whyItMatters: These ideas affect how quickly, reliably, and safely a frontend works.
foundations.browserPerspective: Build tools run during development or deployment; the browser receives their output.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Use one consistent toolchain and pin important versions in the lockfile.
foundations.businessImpact: Fast builds shorten feedback loops and make releases easier to repeat.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Keep configuration understandable and align local builds with CI.
foundations.performanceImpact: Inspect production output and measure page performance instead of assuming optimization.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A development server proves production works
commonMisconceptions.reality: Test the production build and deployment path separately.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A bundler always makes the app faster
commonMisconceptions.reality: Poor splitting or duplicated packages can create larger or slower output.
